criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-BND-01 has `mechanism` naming crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs (not "none"), keeps owner Themis, and `measure` ends with `status: not shown` plus the name of the showing test (git diff docs/spec.toml).
criteria.evidence: The diff changes only the mechanism and measure lines. The mechanism names `guard_origin_write` in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs and `Git::own_origin_url` in athena-git. The owner is still "Themis". The measure names `gh::tests::git_remote_refuses_writes_to_any_remote_but_origin` and ends with `status: not shown`. The test `oly_b_bnd_01_names_the_origin_guard_as_its_mechanism` passed: it parses the real spec file, checks measure_problem is None, checks that the named test exists, and checks that spec_gaps has no entry for the id.

criteria.criterion: Grep finds the guard function in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs and its use in GitRemote push, replace and delete_branch; crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs push_branch/push_if_remote_at are guarded to origin.
criteria.evidence: In remote.rs, `fn guard_origin_write` is called on the first line of `push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`, before `self.git.run`. In athena-git/src/lib.rs, `self.own_origin_url(remote)?` is the first line of both `push_if_remote_at` and `push_branch`. Grepping crates/ for every caller of push_branch, push_if_remote_at and GitLandingRecords::for_remote shows they all pass the literal "origin".

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test builds a temp repo with bare `origin` and `upstream` remotes, calls GitRemote push, replace and delete_branch with name `upstream`, asserts an error and unchanged upstream refs, and the same calls to `origin` succeed.
criteria.evidence: `git_remote_refuses_writes_to_any_remote_but_origin ... ok`. It first runs a control: a raw `git push upstream` that lands. Then push, replace and delete_branch to `upstream` and to a third remote `mirror` each return an error with refs unchanged. The same three calls to origin succeed, and the test checks this with remote_head. The athena-git twin `pushes_reach_only_origin_and_a_push_to_any_other_remote_is_refused` passed under `cargo test --release -p athena-git`. I used the release profile because the debug build reused a stale athena-git artifact (see summary).

criteria.evidence: All of these passed: git_remote_with_no_origin_refuses_and_writes_nothing, a_local_path_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call (with the control a_single_url_github_origin_reaches_the_early_steps), origin_repository_reads_only_the_parsed_owner_and_repo, git_remote_refuses_a_doubled_push_url (asserts git lists two push URLs), git_remote_refuses_a_doubled_fetch_url (asserts there is no pushurl and two push URLs), git_remote_refuses_a_push_url_naming_another_repository, a_doubled_github_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call and a_mismatched_github_push_url_makes_no_host_or_remote_call. In athena-git, all 70 tests pass, including the new doubled-URL, mismatched-URL, URL-spelling and hook-declined tests.

criteria.criterion: The new tests assert on the refusal (error and unchanged refs), so removing the guard call from GitRemote::push makes a test fail; the diff shows this and not only wiring.
criteria.evidence: `assert_writes_refused` calls `remote.push(...)`, then `result.unwrap_err()`, checks the error text, and compares the refs of both bare repositories before and after. If the guard call were removed from push, the push to upstream would land, so unwrap_err would panic and the refs comparison would fail. findings.summary: `athena land --pr` now refuses ssh and scp-style GitHub origins, which a user with such an origin will feel.
findings.evidence: Before, land_pr used `parse_remote(&url)`. Now it uses `own_origin_repository`, which accepts only an https github.com URL, and the test asserts that `ssh://github.com/example/project.git` is refused. The plan accepted this and the CHANGELOG states it. A simpler alternative would map ssh and scp-style GitHub URLs to owner/repo, since the single-URL and same-repository checks already confine where writes can go.

findings.summary: In this snapshot, a debug-profile build reuses a stale athena-git artifact, so `cargo test -p athena-core --lib gh::tests` fails to compile. This comes from the build cache, not the candidate.
findings.evidence: In the first run, cargo recompiled athena-gate and athena-core but not athena-git, and failed with E0432 "no `OWN_REMOTE` in the root" even though the source defines it. A fresh `--release` build compiled and passed, and CI passed on this commit.

summary: The change does what the retry asked. Every push, replace and branch delete Athena makes now goes through one check: `guard_origin_write` in remote.rs, which calls `Git::own_origin_url` in athena-git. That check refuses any remote not named origin, a missing origin, an origin with more than one fetch or push URL, and a push URL that names a different repository from the fetch URL. The pull request calls in `land_pr` and in the early PR and CI-branch steps read the target repository from that same checked origin. OLY-B-BND-01 in docs/spec.toml now names this guard as its mechanism and its measure ends with `status: not shown`. I ran the new tests under the release profile and they all pass: 140 gh tests in athena-core and 70 in athena-git. They push for real to temporary bare repositories and check that refused writes leave every ref unchanged; each refusal test also has a control step where the write succeeds. One note on the build: my first debug-profile run failed to compile, because cargo reused a stale build of athena-git from before the change. The source does define `OWN_REMOTE` and `own_origin_url`, the clean release build passed, and CI recorded fmt, clippy and the full test suite as passing on this commit, so this is a build-cache problem in the snapshot, not in the candidate. Only the 7 listed files changed. There is one minor finding: `athena land --pr` now refuses ssh and scp-style GitHub origins. That was planned and the CHANGELOG states it, but users with an ssh origin will see their landings refused.
